data.narrative:
Westmag is a seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by David Hansen and Jordan Sanders. The firm has raised $11M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a sector universe of nine robotics and manufacturing peers (one public, eight private), including companies such as Walden Robotics, Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, and Generalist AI.

The stage-progression method is the primary applicable approach here. Using the $11M total raised as a proxy for current value and applying a 2.5x multiplier typical of seed-to-next-stage advancement yields an implied valuation of $28M. A peer-median cross-check proved inapplicable due to insufficient narrow-stage comparables: while the robotics and manufacturing sector contains ten same-sector peers, only one matched seed-stage criteria, falling short of the three-datapoint threshold needed for statistical reliability. Reliance on all-sector medians would introduce unacceptable noise given the limited near-peer dataset.

The triangulation supports a valuation range of $23M to $32M, with a median point of $28M. This range reflects a narrow evidential base—only one applied method—and carries material uncertainty around appropriate step-up multiples for this particular stage and sector. Key assumptions requiring validation include whether the 2.5x multiplier accurately reflects Westmag's risk profile relative to typical seed progressions, and whether the $11M raised appropriately proxies intrinsic value absent operational metrics or revenue data.
